boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen LaFourche Crossing record (June 20-21, 1863) in Taylor's Operations in West Louisiana [June-September 1863]. The live campaign label reads Taylor's Operations in Louisiana West of Mississip[pi]. The capture of Thibodeaux on June 20 and of Brashear City on June 23 are context. Campaign-wide movements (Major's raid, the capture of Brashear City and Bayou Boeuf, the river batteries of July 3-10, the withdrawal to the Teche and the September operations) and multi-action totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 838 men from eight regiments [US] and 2nd Cavalry Brigade [CS]; the frozen Union bound is 838 and the live field reads 838 total (US 838; CS 0). Stickney says his force was about 502 on the evening of June 20, that Sawtell arrived with 306 men that night, and that his actual force in the fight was 838, of whom only about 600 were engaged; he estimates the Confederates in the charge at about 600. Irwin repeats the 838 by organization, says Major reported Pyron's attacking regiment as 206 strong, and that Cahill's arrival on June 22 gave Stickney about 1,100 (printed 'i,icxD' in OCR).
claims.rationale: Stickney's 838 is a force present on June 21 and his 600 an engaged estimate; the Confederate figures differ (600 estimated against 206 reported for one regiment). Irwin repeats Stickney's 838. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live Confederate zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 267 total (US 48; CS 219); the live field reads 268 total (US 49; CS 219). Stickney's table totals 8 killed and 41 wounded (49); he counted 53 Confederate dead inside the pickets, found nearly 60 wounded at Thibodeaux, and inferred a loss of about 300 killed and wounded from an assumed ratio. Irwin gives 8 and 41 and quotes a regimental history's 108 dead delivered and 40 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Stickney's 300 is his inference, not a count.

open_questions: Emory's No. 1 reports, Grow's No. 4, Major's No. 12, Cahill's and the Confederate casualty returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' assistant adjutant-general. Its chapters cite and quote Stickney's and Green's reports, so it is not independent of them. Stickney's July 9, 1863 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XXVI, Part 1, a shared container) is one interested Union family. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
